chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: The automatic bootblack chair and the portable barber chair
summary: Spikes describes a hydraulic bootblack chair with a shine counter, shown at an inventors' exhibit until the war stopped production, and a bicycle-mounted barber chair.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Here's an automatic bootblack chair that he invented. You see, when this is down--like this--that's the way it stands--these legs out, and say a woman wanted to get on there, she steps on there, and he just shine and press the button and it runs up like this, and the foot pieces come in, and you don't have to climb up and down. And then when you get through, you press the button, and it goes back down, and you step off.
Yeah. You see, that...that's when it's up, and that's when it's down. Now I had that into the Biltmore...

Inventors' Commissioner...uh...Institution for a week, and I had quite a few sales, and I took it all the way back to New York, and I had quite a few sales but then the war come...couldn't get material to make it. But it was a purty thing, and that's a...it's all hydraulic, You see, you press a button, and then it had a register over here how many times it shines--how many shines you made a day. In case a man had a bootblack stand and had ten or twelve boys working in there, he go on about his business and come back at night and check up just like a cash register: You got twenty sales today-- you got twenty shines today. You see?
Very clever. So that was...was that, you say...
You said the war came so that was what-- that was done in the late '30s, maybe?
Yeah. Well, whenever the war was. When was it?
Well, we got into it in '41.

Yeah. Well, you see, this is what I was telling you--you see how he carried that little box there all the tubes, and it just had a bicycle leg on it, and drive...ride it around, and you got your tools right there, and you cut your hair, and you sit all down on there.
And that's the Spikes barber chair.
That is very clever. 'Foot or hand-controlled. Adjustable to any position instantly.'
You see there. I guess that's the copyright number, isn't it?
2,517,936 Patent Number. That's what it says.
